issues.sym: Reverse suddenly disappears or feels shaky, the engine races on shifts as if stuck in a high gear, or the transmission stops engaging and the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: A wave plate (a spring-like clutch part) inside the 6-speed automatic can crack and break. GM issued special coverage (bulletin 14404) for 2007-2009 Outlooks, but that 10-year/120,000-mile coverage has now run out. Transmission failure is the most-reported problem on the Outlook.
issues.next: If Reverse goes missing or the transmission starts slipping, stop driving it hard and have it diagnosed right away. Caught early, the broken part can sometimes be replaced during an overhaul instead of replacing the whole transmission.

issues.sym: Check engine light with timing codes such as P0008, P0009 or P0016-P0019. The engine may rattle on start-up or run rough.
issues.why: The timing chains on both versions of the 3.6L V6 stretch early, and tensioners and guides wear. Low or old oil speeds it up. GM's extended coverage for this (11340C) has expired.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm the cause before replacing sensors. The proper fix is all three chains, the guides and tensioners together. Driving on a badly stretched chain risks major engine damage.

issues.t: Hard steering at low speeds from a failing power steering pump
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets very heavy, mostly when parking or turning slowly, then may go back to normal. Topping up the fluid doesn't fix it.
issues.why: The power steering pump wears out, and fluid leaks from the steering rack can speed that up. Some owners had pumps replaced under GM special coverage; others found no leak and no clear cause.
issues.next: Treat sudden heavy steering as a safety issue. Have the pump pressure and the rack checked for leaks, and ask a GM dealer with your VIN whether any coverage applies.

issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips under the front, the fluid level keeps dropping, and steering assist cuts out at low speed.
issues.why: Seals in the rack-and-pinion steering gear leak. The leak can contaminate the fluid and lead to pump failure too.
issues.next: Have the rack inspected. Fixing a leaking rack early can save the pump.

issues.t: Low-beam headlight burns out repeatedly from melted wiring
issues.sym: One low-beam headlight keeps going out, sometimes right after a new bulb; lights flicker, and there may be a burnt smell near the headlight.
issues.why: The headlight connector and wiring overheat and melt or burn. Owners believe the wiring is too light for the heat and current. This is the most common complaint filed with NHTSA for the Outlook.
issues.next: If a bulb keeps failing, check the connector for browning or melting. Have the damaged plug and wiring replaced, not just the bulb.

issues.t: Water leaks from clogged sunroof drains damage electronics
issues.sym: Water drips from the headliner or soaks the footwells after rain, and odd electrical faults follow: airbag warning lights, dead speakers, blower, window or lighting failures, and even stalling.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog, so rainwater overflows into the cabin and runs down to fuse boxes, modules and wiring, corroding them.
issues.next: Have the sunroof drains cleared and tested as soon as you find water. Dry the carpet fully and have any wet modules or connectors checked before corrosion spreads.

issues.t: Misfire and surging from failing ignition coils
issues.sym: Surging or bucking under load, at highway speed or on hills, a feeling that the transmission is hunting between gears, and a check engine light with misfire codes.
issues.why: Ignition coils fail early, likely because of engine heat. Replacing one coil often lets another one fail soon after.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and the coils tested. Many owners replace all six coils (and the spark plugs) at once.

issues.t: Liftgate struts can weaken and let the gate fall (recall)
issues.sym: The open liftgate drifts down or falls on its own, and could hit someone.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold the liftgate up wear out. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 15V-415).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Heated washer module can short and catch fire (recalls)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, other electrical features acting up, or the heated washer not working.
issues.why: The heated windshield washer module can short circuit. GM first recalled it (NHTSA 08V-441) and later recalled it again to disable the module (NHTSA 10V-240).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Service Air Bag warning from seat wiring (recall)
issues.sym: The Service Air Bag light comes on. The side airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: Wiring connectors under the front seats can lose good contact. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 14V-118) to fix the connections.
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Front seat belt cable can break (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you would notice while driving. In a crash, the front seat belt may not hold properly.
issues.why: The flexible steel cable that anchors the front belt buckle can wear and separate over time. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 14V-266).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Wipers may stop working in heavy snow or ice (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers quit during heavy snow or ice buildup.
issues.why: The wiper linkage can come apart under heavy load. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 08V-410).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Second-row seat belt may not restrain properly (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing obvious. In a crash, the second-row belt may not hold the occupant as designed.
issues.why: Interior trim can interfere with the second-row seat belt. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 10V-375).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Vehicle may roll away after shifting to Park (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle may not restart, or may roll after you get out, because the transmission isn't fully in Park.
issues.why: A shift cable part may not have been fully seated at the factory. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 09V-073).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle may be missing a rivet (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you would notice. In a crash, the buckle could separate from its strap.
issues.why: Some buckle assemblies were built without a rivet. GM recalled the vehicles (NHTSA 08V-615).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.

issues.sym: Usually nothing you would notice. The front airbags may not work as intended in a crash.
issues.why: The airbag sensing module on some early 2007 Outlooks needed new software. GM recalled them (NHTSA 07V-062).
issues.next: Check your VIN on a recall lookup or ask a GM dealer. The repair is free if it was never done.
